title: MIRR compounds positive NPV by full cashflow count n rather than n - 1 and diverges up to 9.6 ULP on two-flow calls
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527, MIRR(values, finance_rate, reinvest_rate) computes positive_npv using NPV's x87-staged loop, multiplies it by pow(1 + reinvest_rate, n) (over all n entries rather than n - 1), checks a zero finance divisor (#DIV/0!) before final normalization overflow except when a positive term itself overflows (#NUM!), and takes the (n - 1)-th root via pow(-grown_positive / finance_pv, 1 / (n - 1)) - 1. Because of the extra divide-and-multiply by (1 + reinvest_rate) and x87 staging, MIRR({-100, 110}, -1, 0.1) returns 0.09999999999999987 (0x3fb9999999999990), 9.6 ULP below 0.1.
basis: Measured across 3,475 full-bank MIRR rows in Excel 16.0.20527 (17 triage rows in crates/calc-func/witness-reference/MIRR.tsv; 3,458/3,475 matched) and prefix_metadata (row 370).

correct.how: Exact algebraic MIRR((-100, 110), -1, 0.1) = 110/100 - 1 = 0.1 rounded to nearest binary64
